thread.title: Samsung Provides More Evidence Of Weak iPhone X Sales

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Samsung Provides More Evidence Of Weak iPhone X Sales
text:
South Korean electronics giant Samsung on Thursday warned about a slowdown in its display panel segment, likely in part to declining OLED screen orders from Apple ( AAPL ) for its flagship iPhone X handset.
X Samsung also said profitability in its smartphone business will take a hit from heightened competition in the premium segment of the handset market, where it mostly butts heads with Apple.
"Generating overall earnings growth across the company will be a challenge due to weakness in the display panel segment and a decline in profitability in the mobile business amid rising competition in the high-end segment," Samsung said in a written statement .
Samsung's first-quarter results got a lift from the launch of its new flagship smartphone, the Galaxy S9. But the company sees profitability declining in its mobile business in the second quarter from the first. It cited "stagnant sales of flagship models amid weak demand."

Chipmakers such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ( TSM ) have signaled slowing orders for smartphone chips through at least the first half of 2018.
Samsung expects to see a rebound in demand for OLED smartphone panels in the second half of the year. Apple is rumored to be introducing two new OLED-screen iPhones in September. Samsung makes organic light-emitting diode screens for its own smartphones and also supplies them to Apple for the iPhone X.
Apple reportedly has slashed production of the iPhone X amid weak sales. Analysts say many consumers are turned off by its premium price, which starts at $999. They also dinged its lack of must-have new features.
"While not directly commenting on Apple, Samsung's rhetoric suggested the iPhone X remained weak in Q1 and should remain challenging in Q2," Cowen analyst Karl Ackerman said in a note to clients. "This is in-line with our iPhone build checks for Q1 and Q2, and this underscores our work since last December when we were one of the first to point out iPhone X builds being curtailed and back-filled by older models."
Samsung Helped By Memory Chips Samsung also predicted continued strong performance from its memory chip business, which has been its main revenue and profit driver. It sees solid demand for DRAM and Nand memory chips for data centers and smartphones.
Memory chips have been "the saving grace" for Samsung, investment firm Semiconductor Advisors said in a report Thursday. The memory business "is so strong that it easily overpowers even the bad handset news."
Memory-chip stocks rose following Samsung's report. Micron Technology ( MU ) jumped 5.3% to close at 50.14 on the stock market today . Western Digital ( WDC ) climbed 2.3% to 87.91.
